characters.description: The Ageless: Ghosts age under normal circumstances, and their apparent age seems to reflect their mindset. That said, they still seem to be immune to theeffectsof aging.Desiree was clearly stated to have died of old age. However, after her death, she has remained an outwardly youthful ghost for centuries.Sidney Poindexter, a teen who died inThe '50s, clearly hasn't age since his demise.Box Lunch, daughter of the Box Ghost and the Lunch Lady, is a young child despite being born a ghost but doesn't appear to mature beyond that. Desiree was clearly stated to have died of old age. However, after her death, she has remained an outwardly youthful ghost for centuries. Sidney Poindexter, a teen who died inThe '50s, clearly hasn't age since his demise. Box Lunch, daughter of the Box Ghost and the Lunch Lady, is a young child despite being born a ghost but doesn't appear to mature beyond that. Alien Blood: Apparently, ghosts (and half ghosts in their ghost forms) bleed glowing green ectoplasm, as shown in "Fright Knight" whenDanny gets a cut by a blade.◊

characters.name: Danny Fenton/Danny Phantom
characters.description: The main hero of the series. Upon obtaining his ghost powers through aFreak Lab Accident, 14-year old Danny uses it to combat the various ghosts that inhabit hishometown. He starts off shy, naive,Book Dumb, and emotional, constantly trying to find a place in the world, whether it be gaining popularity or through his ghost powers. By the end of the series, Dannygains confidence, courage, and matures considerably, and finds his path as a hero. Acquired Situational Narcissism: In the episode where he became filthy rich. All Guys Want Cheerleaders: Danny constantly moons over theegotistical and vainPaulina,although he eventually realizes that she's not worth his time. All of the Other Reindeer: Danny is patronized and sometimes ignored by his family (especially his sister), bullied and ostracized at his school (to the point of being him and his friends being theonlyones not invited to major social events), and feared and hated in his superhero identity by both most mortals and ghosts. Fortunately, his best friends help keep him steady while the world, starting with his sister, gradually begins to come around. Amazon Chaser: Apparently, he inherited this from his father.He has a huge amount ofUSTwith hischildhood friend, Sam Manson, aBadass Normal.Danny's response to Sam's concerns about himDating Catwoman? "I know [Valerie] wants to waste Danny Phantom... but did you know that she's a ninth-degree black belt?"

characters.name: Sam Manson
characters.description: Danny's childhood friend and primary love interest. Sam is a strict vegetarianGothwith an often contradictory personality; she's as rational and levelheaded as she is forceful and selfish. She strives to protect the environment as much as she rebels against her parents. She often keeps Danny (and Tucker) from doing anything too extreme. Action Survivor: Despite all she goes through, she manages to survive many of the ghost attacks. Animal Lover: She prides herself on caring about and protecting all animals, from refusing to dissect frogs for biology and trying to set a gorilla free from a zoo. Animal Motif: While spiders and bats are a given with her Goth lifestyle, her spider backpack and eating gummi bats being standouts, the animal she's more akin to is cats. She mentions in "Shades of Gray" that she's a cat person. While she meant she prefers cats to dogs, her personality is much like that of a cat: she's a picky eater, she's independent, and very selective of who she associates with. Animal Wrongs Group: In "One of A Kind", she wants to set the Purpleback gorilla free from the zoo, making Danny do an essay to prove why it deserves to roam free since there's only two left in the world. Even ignoring that the gorilla is more than likely in the zoobecauseit's endangered and to prevents poachers and predators from doing harm, she lets the gorilla free under the mistaken idea it wants out (when in fact it notices Skulker and is trying to warn her) and, as far as Danny and Tucker knew, was about to attack them. She blackmails them with a photo of them hugging while asleep to keep world of her letting the gorilla go a secret.

characters.name: Tucker Foley
characters.description: Danny's childhood friend"since forever", Tucker is a Techno Geek whoconsiders himself God's gift not only to women, but to all humankind. Acquired Situational Narcissism: Whenever he gets a lot of power, he turns into a megalomaniac. This is best seen in the episodes where he gets his own ghost powers and where he was made king of the world. Action Survivor: Like Sam, despite being less capable in a fight than her. Berserk Button: He doesn't like being separated from technology. Big Eater: Will eat anything,except vegetables.

characters.name: Jazz Fenton
characters.description: Danny's older sister is an intelligent 16-year old who claims to be an adult trapped in a teenager's body. As such, she's often playing aparentalrole towards her entire family, trying to lead her parents into normality and shielding a then unsure Danny from the harsh realities of the outside world. After finding out ghosts are indeed real and Danny'sSecret Identity, she slowly gains admiration for her growing brother and eventually becomes part of "Team Phantom". She eventually lets down her shield and slowly starts to act her age, all the while happily acknowledging her love for ghosts — at several times, becoming aBadass Bookworm. #1 Dime: Bearbert Einstein, a teddy bear withAlbert Einstein's face which she's had since she was little. Ripping out its stuffing is enough to make her descend into the childlike mindset needed to see Youngblood. Academic Alpha Bitch: BeforeCharacter Development, she considered herself too good for her family because of how intelligent and mature she was. All Girls Want Bad Boys: This was part of her initial attraction to Johnny 13. Amateur Therapist: Jazz likes to read psychology books in her spare time, and so sometimes has decent advice for those around her. This is especially pronounced in "Reality Trip" when she helps her parents unpack why Danny never told them about his secret identity, which helps them to be supportive once they reunite with Danny again. She also diagnoses Freakshow with "ghost envy", a term she coined for her college admissions essay to refer to humans who are jealous of ghosts to the point they wish theywereghosts (something she herself is intimately familiar with). She talks to him about his childhood being upstaged by ghosts at his family's circus, and he feels understood by her.Subverted in that Jazz then tells Danny about this weakness, which he uses to defeat Freakshow.

characters.name: Vlad Masters/Plasmius
characters.description: 0% Approval Rating:Becomes this at the end of the series after his finalEvil PlantoTake Over the Worldfails, as having already unveiled his true nature to the world, he knows he is now an enemy of Earth and can never go back, especially now that even Jack hates him, and is left to roam for eternity in space alone. Abhorrent Admirer: When he reveals to Maddie that he wants her to leave Jack for him, she ended up hating his guts. Aborted Arc: Whatever plans he had for the Ghost King's Crown and partnership with the Fright Knight were ultimately abandoned in Season 3 after the show's former head of story left.In the graphic novelDanny Phantom: A Glitch in Time, when the two meet again, the Fright Knight claims he no longer serves him and attacks his former master, implying the two had some kind of a fallout after Vlad's banishment. In the graphic novelDanny Phantom: A Glitch in Time, when the two meet again, the Fright Knight claims he no longer serves him and attacks his former master, implying the two had some kind of a fallout after Vlad's banishment. Abusive Parents: He created Danielle, who was loyal to and desired affection from him. However, he treated her as a mindless, disposable drone and verbally abuses her whenever she questions his orders. Their "relationship" only worsens when Vlad tries tomelt her aliveto study her remains, and even before that,she renounces all ties with himafter realizing he only saw her as "a mess he's not gonna clean up".

characters.name: Pariah Dark
characters.description: Absolute ruler of the Ghost Zoneuntil he wasdefeated and imprisoned, Pariah is far and away one of the most powerful characters to appear in the series, to the extent of effortlessly owning Vlad within seconds of being freed and commanding the allegiance of Fright Knight, another tremendously powerful villain. He was inadvertently released by Vlad, who was looking for hisartifacts of doom, the Ring of Rage and Crown of Fire, and immediately proceeded to conquer both the Ghost Zone and Amity Park. Ultimately, Danny was able to seal him again (with some help), but the Ghost King was not destroyed and may yet be free to walk the world again. 0% Approval Rating: Absolutelynoneof the ghosts like him and The Fright Knight only seems to serve him out of fear.Fits since his name is Pariah, which means something that is despised or avoided. Bad Boss: He constantly menaces the Fright Knight into submission. At one point he even fires a ghost ray at Vlad while the Fright Knight is still standing right next to him, injuring him in the process. One can hardly blame The Knight for eventually turning against Pariah at the end of the episode. Big Bad: Of the first TV movie,Reign Storm. After being freed from the sarcophagus by Vlad, Dark Pariah restarts his campaign of conquest, beginning with Amity Park, which ends up making him a threat not only to Planet Earth, but also to the Phantom Zone. Brought Down to Badass: Pariah loses his ring and crown, which enhance his power, at the start of the special. But, he still curbstomps everyone in the show.

characters.name: Dark Danny
characters.description: Dark Danny is the main antagonist ofThe Ultimate Enemy. Danny'salternate futurecounterpart through a fusion between his ghost half and Vlad's after an accident that renders hisfamily, friends, and teacher deadfrom aNasty Burgerexplosion. He is a straight-to-the-point villain who creates mayhem and destruction in his path with absolutely no guilt for his cause. He is perhaps the most dangerous villain in the show because of hispersonal natureand utter depravity. 0% Approval Rating: He is hated by all remaining humans and the various ghosts that comprised hisRogues Galleryas a teen for terrorizing the Earthandthe Ghost Zone. The disdain for him is so strong that the younger version of Danny was attacked by Valerie and the other ghosts simply for either resembling his future counterpart or being a weaker version of him they could defeat in his counterpart's place. Aborted Arc: The last moments of "The Ultimate Enemy" hinted that he would one day break free, but this never happened. Supposedly, Steve Marmel's plans while he was still part of the show were for Dark Danny to return as theFinal Bossof the series. However, he would later finally return inDanny Phantom: A Glitch in Time. Actually, I Am Him:Jack:Where is he? Where's our son?!Maddie:What have you done to our boy?!Dark Danny: (laughing maniacally) IAM"your boy"! Adaptation Name Change: The video game adaptation calls himDan Phantom. This name was likely chosen without consent fromButch Hartman, who uses the name "Dark Danny". Technically, neither of these are his actual name, just placeholders to separate him and Danny.

characters.name: Freakshow
characters.description: The ringmaster of Circus Gothica. He traveled the country with his Goth circus, though it was really a cover. The performers, save for his assistant Lydia, were ghosts under the control of his staff. He used his staff to make them steal from the towns they visited. He's also the only human in the series to be a genuine villain. (All other humans that opposed Danny Phantom were either Vlad, who is half-ghost, or ghost hunters whoviewed all ghosts asAlways Chaotic Evil.) Acquired Achilles' Heel:This is how Danny beats him in "Reality Trip:" when Danny learns that Freakshow has ghost envy, he taunts him with his ghostly powers to provoke Freakshow into using theReality Gauntletto turn himself into a powerful ghost..which is what Danny was counting on, because the Fenton Thermos doesn't work on humans, which Freakshow no longer is. Ambiguous Situation: Based on how he doesn't share the hypnotized look on the Guys in White at the end of "Reality Trip", it's unknown if he remembers Danny Phantom's real identity or not. Bad Boss: To all his brainwashed pawns. Lydia's the only one he treats with respect, but that's probably just favoritism due to her being hisImplied Love Interest. Bald of Evil: He doesn't have a lock of hair on his head and is pretty evil.

characters.name: Skulker
characters.description: One of the show's most recurring villains, Skulker is a ghost obsessed with hunting to such an extent that he's considered the Ghost Zone's greatest predator. Growing bored, he looked to the human world for a challenge and fixated on Danny, whose hybrid nature made for an endlessly exciting hunt. In theBad Future, he merged with Technus to become Skulktech 9.9. Anatomy Arsenal: Most of his weapons are built into his mechanical body.Arm Cannon: His most common weapon, he has many varieties of this.Blade Below the Shoulder: Shows up in the episode "Bitter Reunions."Shoulder Cannon: Another common weapon. Arm Cannon: His most common weapon, he has many varieties of this. Blade Below the Shoulder: Shows up in the episode "Bitter Reunions." Shoulder Cannon: Another common weapon.

characters.name: Bertrand
characters.description: Spectra's loyalBattle Butler. Battle Butler: He wears a butler's attire in his standard human form, and he's the one who does most of the fighting for Spectra. Blob Monster: His true form is a green ectoplasmic blob with red eyes. Butt-Monkey: It seems that he's rejected by Johnny and Skulker, who don't invite him to go to Amity Park with them in "Girls' Night Out", and even Spectra seems to hate him in that episode. Camp Straight: He has some effeminate qualities and is just as vain as his boss, but is also implied to be in a relationship with her.

characters.name: Box Ghost
characters.description: AHarmless Villain, Box Ghost's main shtick is anything cardboard and square (and the occasional bubble wrap). Consistently pathetic and easy to beat, he remains determined to be taken seriously. HeTook a Level in Badassin theBad Future, becoming incredibly muscular and gaining the ability to form exploding boxes out of energy. Big Bad Wannabe: Talks a big game, but no one pays much attention to him. Butt-Monkey: Frequently. Skulker likes using him as bait, for starters. Catchphrase: "I am the Box Ghost!" "BEWARE!" A Day in the Limelight: In "Boxed Up Fury", he’s the main villain of the episode.

characters.name: Desiree
characters.description: A ghostgeniewho is forced to grant people's wishes, most of them resulting in a terrible price on the wisher. As a human, Desiree was the favored lover of a sultan's harem, a love she gave back. His jealous wife drove her away, forcing her to remain vindictive and heartbroken throughout the series. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Her attire consists of a tube top. Batman Gambit: At one point, she began stalking Team Phantom when she saw that Danny and Sam were arguing. She was waiting for the point when one of them used the magic words "I wish I never met you!"Without Sam as Danny's friend, he never became Danny Phantom, and Desiree took advantage of this to remove Danny as an obstacle for her plans involvinga meteor shower. Beat It by Compulsion: A drawback to her powers is that she has to granteverywish someone makes in front of her, even if it's a wish that can be used against her (such as wishing she'd be in the Fenton Thermos). Beauty Is Bad: Alongside being aJackass Genie, Desiree is probably one of the few villains to have a sexually-alluring appearance, what with herbuxom figure,long hair, and tone of voice. Not to mention she was once a harem girl.

characters.name: EmberMcLain
characters.description: A punk rock diva, Ember hates all sense of authority and adults. She wants toTake Over the Worldstrictly so people will always remember her name. She tends to be a blunt person. In theBad Future, she isoverweightand her vocal cords have been damaged, rendering her unable to sing. The '70s: She uses '70s lingo, suggesting that she might have lived and died in that time period. Advertised Extra: She was constantly talked up in and out-of-universe as a major recurring rogue. However, she’s definitely more of a secondary villain at best. Her appearances were already pretty few and far between. Out of her six total appearances, she only played a major role in three of them, and she’s not even the star villain in two out of those three episodes. It’s probable that the show just hyped her up so much due to herunexpected popularity with fans. Attention Whore: Invokes this to gain power, simply byhaving her fanssay her name. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Her attire consists of a small crop-top.

characters.name: Fright Knight
characters.description: A ghost considered to be the spirit of Halloween, Fright Knight is a very powerfulSealed Evil in a Caninadvertently released by Danny, who was trying to put together a haunted house as part of a detention for Mr. Lancer. He was resealed at the end of the episode, only to be released later by Pariah to serve asThe Dragon. At the end of "Reign Storm", he was seen to make an alliance with Vlad to take down his master, but this is never really followed up on. In theBad Futureof "The Ultimate Enemy",Dark Dannyseems to have inherited his loyalty. Aborted Arc: The writers clearly planned forsomethingbig to come of his alliance with Vlad, since the whole of "Reign Storm" leads up to it and it's alluded to in "The Ultimate Enemy". But for some reason, it's just sort of forgotten about. And I'm the Queen of Sheba: In theNickelodeon Magazinecomic story "Bring Back My Body to Me", Danny in Vlad's body tries to convince the Fright Knight that he isn't Vlad. The Fright Knight retorts "AndIamJorgen Von Strangle". Armor Is Useless: Utterly subverted, giving him extra protection and being one of Danny's toughest opponents. Artifact of Doom: His sword, the Soulshredder.

characters.name: The Guys in White
characters.description: Anti-Hero: While "hero" is a bit of a stretch, the Guys in White are not antagonistic for personal gain; they're government operatives carrying out security and executive policy. However, they're overzealous to the point they don't care about collateral damage they cause, and they're committed to the extermination of ghosts, going so far as to plotting to destroy the entire Ghost Zone (which would've destroyed the Earth as well). Ascended Extra: Introduced in late season one as minor villains and pawns in Vlad's plan who are total jokes. Starting in late season 2, they're more active and much bigger threats to Danny. Corrupted Character Copy: They're visually based on Agents J and K from theMen In Blackfilms, but they lack the two's camaraderie, morals, and competency. They also seeallghosts as monsters, whereas J and K know not all aliens are threats to the Earth. Determinator: They are shown obsessed with hunting down their primary target, Danny Phantom. When they temporarily discovered hisSecret Identity, they relentlessly chased him and his friends across the country from Florida, Nevada, to San Diego in a blind effort to destroy and dissect him. They are also determined to destroy all ghosts in existence, even the Ghost Zone (not knowing that if the Ghost Zone is destroyed, the Earth gets destroyed as well). Evil Hero: They're this by virtue of trying to fight ghosts, yet constantly trying to also stop Danny Phantom. They even believe that they're the good guys as theydress in white.

characters.name: Johnny  13
characters.description: A scruffy punk on a motorcycle. His main goals are raising havoc and pleasing his girlfriend, Kitty. In theBad Future, he is in a wheelchair. 13 Is Unlucky: His name and powers are correlated. Badass Biker: Has a spectral motorbike that he uses both as transportation and as a weapon. Chain Pain: He briefly wields one in "Livin' Large" when threatening Danny. Chivalrous Pervert: While he loves Kitty very much, he can't help ogling the ladies, infuriating her to no end.

characters.name: Kitty
characters.description: Johnny 13's girlfriend. She mostly follows his path, but can be quite dangerous, especially when she's angry. She seemed the least changed in theBad Future, but joined Johnny and the others in attempting revenge. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Why Kitty is attracted to Johnny 13. Anti-Villain: She's one of the least villainous ghosts Danny deals with, as she apologized to Danny for causing him trouble once. However, she still causes trouble, either to teach Johnny a lesson or make Amity Park suitable only for women. Artifact of Doom: Her scarf, jacket and ring are artifacts she can use to transform the body of any human woman who wears them into her host. Clingy Jealous Girl:Reallyhates it when Johnny is looking at other women besides her.

characters.name: Lunch Lady
characters.description: Her goal is to serve food to everybody, but she goes into a homicidal rage if people refuse. She doesn't like vegetables. Affably Evil: Despite her lack of morals, she's sweet and grandmotherly — well,sometimes. Angry Chef: Gets really ticked off when people change her menus. Apron Matron: Can go from kind and motherly when offering food to vicious and bloodthirsty when her food is rejected. Berserk Button: Changing the Casper High cafeteria menu will drive her insane, but either accepting or refusing the food she randomly offers to people in the middle of her fights also works.

characters.name: Lydia
characters.description: Freakshow's right-hand woman and the only ghost in his team who serves him willingly. She never speaks. She is able to bring the tattoos on her body to life and send them to attack people. Animated Tattoo: She is able to bring the tattoos on her body to life and send them to attack people. Beauty Is Bad: Lydia is an attractive villainess, featuring a unique design and decent exposure. The Dragon: To Freakshow. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: When Danny traps Freakshow in the Fenton Thermos, she'sabsolutely furious.

characters.name: Penelope Spectra
characters.description: On the outside, Spectra looks to be a kind, perky woman who just wants to help teenagers and their depression. In reality, she is aVain Sorceressghost who sucks in their emotions to further her youth and beauty. Beneath that bubbly personality, Spectra is sadistic and immoral. Battleaxe Nurse: Given that she runs a fake hospital just to torture Danny and his classmates. Beauty Is Bad: Beauty is the sole reason for her villainy, at least for her human form. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Pretends to be a caring psychologist when she really is out only for herself. Break Them by Talking: A very defining trait of hers. She often tries demoralizing her opponents since she needs negativity to function.

characters.name: Sidney Poindexter
characters.description: The ghost of a student at Casper High from the 1950s, Poindexter was stuffed into his locker so many times that he now haunts it. Having been bullied for most of his life, he makes a point to stand up for victims of bullying. Ambiguously Human:There was a Sidney Poindexter who attended the school, but it's a little unclear if he's a dead kid or some sort of manifestation of the real Poindexter's emotions. The fact that he's surrounded by other ghosts who possibly resemble his classmates from the '50s complicates this.As many fans point out, despite his origin, Poindexter actually gives some leeway to the idea that the ghosts in the series aren't spirits of the dead. The fact that he switched bodies with Danny suggests he, well,has a body. There was a Sidney Poindexter who attended the school, but it's a little unclear if he's a dead kid or some sort of manifestation of the real Poindexter's emotions. The fact that he's surrounded by other ghosts who possibly resemble his classmates from the '50s complicates this. As many fans point out, despite his origin, Poindexter actually gives some leeway to the idea that the ghosts in the series aren't spirits of the dead. The fact that he switched bodies with Danny suggests he, well,has a body. Anti-Villain: He's only villainous in his first appearance, and that's because he saw Danny getting back at Dash and jumped to conclusions. Otherwise, he's just a nerdy ghost who just doesn't like bullies. In fact, after his first appearance, he actuallyhelpsDanny every time he appears.

characters.name: Technus
characters.description: Another common enemy, Technus is an eccentric ghost with formidable technological powers and the goal of WORLD DOMINATION — who gets defeated in every appearance, largely due to his bad habit of shouting his plans at the top of his lungs (though his upgrade into Technus 2.0 helped him break that habit). Nonetheless, as long as he can possess sufficiently advanced machinery, he can be quite formidable. In theBad Future, he merged with Skulker to become Skulktech 9.9. All There in the Manual: His first name is never stated in the show, instead being revealed in his character bio in the video game adaption of "The Ultimate Enemy." Beware the Silly Ones: Technus is a hammy, silly villain who monologues a lot, but he's also a genuinely dangerous fighter and can fight Danny quite well even in his early appearances. Cloud Cuckoolander: Prior to being upgraded his plans were skewed towards the bizarre. Cool Shades: Square ones that seem to lack a nosepiece.

characters.name: Walker
characters.description: A ghostly sheriff obsessed with maintaining order at any cost, Walker doesn't have as many appearances as some of the other Rogues' Gallery members, but is still a very significant villain for being the one who reveals the existence of ghosts to the world at large and is responsible for Danny's people initial rep as aHero with Bad Publicity. Badass Normal: Compare to the rest of Danny's rogue gallery, Walker doesn't have any unique skills other than standard ghost powers and being backed up by his guards. Despite this, Walker is one of Danny's most difficult recurring enemy that even aftertaking several levels in badass, he still needs help from Sam and Wulf to defeat him. The Bad Guy Wins:His scheme to discredit Danny in "Public Enemies" actually succeeds, despite Maddie sending him back to the Ghost Zone.Played straight before he is sent back into the Ghost Zone and taunts Danny on how he's made Danny an initial enemy of both his hometown and the Ghost World.Walker:Feared on Earth and Wanted in the Ghost Zone! You've lost, Ghost Kid! LOST! Bald of Evil: In "Call of the Wild", the top of his hat is destroyed, revealing he's bald underneath. Catchphrase: “That’s against the rules.”

characters.name: Youngblood
characters.description: A little, immature boy who likes to play dress up. Despite his size and youth, he can be incredibly dangerous. Affably Evil: As seen in "Livin' Large", he seems to be geniunely friendly to Danny despite them being enemies (when he's not trying to kill Danny and his family just for fun, and when Danny isn't interrupting his evil plans). Ax-Crazy: He spends almost the entirety of "The Fenton Menace" trying to kill the Fentons for fun. Babysitter's Nightmare: TheNickelodeon Magazinecomic story "Brat's Entertainment" has Danny, Sam and Tucker tasked with babysitting Youngblood by his gigantic parents. He proves to be as troublesome and dangerous as he is when Danny fights him, but the three manage to keep him in line by rebuilding his Construct Blocks robot into a cage to hold him in. Beware the Silly Ones: He behaves like a typical brat, often loses himself in his characters and loves to make childish jokes, but he's a dangerous enemy nonetheless, and somehow he's the leader of a crew of ghost pirates.

characters.name: Amorpho
characters.description: A shapeshifting ghost with no face who comes to Amity Park in the episode "Forever Phantom" Anti-Villain: He's not diabolical, just a faceless ghost who enjoys attention and pulling pranks. He also does have standards as he draws the line at killing. He was even willing to call a truce with Danny to cure themselves of theirShapeshifter Mode Lockand evade the mob. Attention Whore: The reason he pulls his stunts is for the attention. Celebrity is Overrated: He shifts into Danny for attention, but quickly learns throughout his debut episode that there's such a thing as "too much attention" and comes to respect Danny and his need of a private life away from the mob. Even Evil Has Standards: Amorpho may have not a care if someone gets angry or slightly hurt by his pranks, but he draws the line at killing, stating that a bus plunging off a cliff was "a tad out of hand" and is thankful Danny Phantom was able to save them.

characters.name: Box Lunch
characters.description: From theBad Future, she is the daughter of Box Ghost and Lunch Lady. Borrowed Catchphrase: She uses her father's "BEWARE!" catchphrase. She even lampshades it.Box Lunch:And now, and you probably know this was coming, BEWARE! Combat Pragmatist: Danny assumes that she's as much of a pushover as her parents, but she uses tactics like closing the gap while Danny is occupied dodging her food and boxes so she can hit him. Cute Bruiser: She's just a child, but manages to put up a decent fight against Danny. Girlish Pigtails: The hairstyle she wears.

characters.name: Ghost Writer
characters.description: A one-shot villain from theChristmas Episode, he tried to get revenge on Danny for accidentally destroying one of his poems. Anti-Villain: Not evil per se, as Dannywasa jerk towards him after learning the book he'd accidentally incinerated was aChristmaspoem. Card-Carrying Villain: At one point, he says that he’s really quite wicked when he gets the urge. Didn't See That Coming:He didn't foreseethe other villains teaming up with Danny to take him downfor having the audacity to attack someone on Christmas. Disproportionate Retribution: He trapped Danny in a book where everyone was against him just because Danny destroyed his poem. Granted, Danny was very rude and unapologetic about it once he learned it was a Christmas poem.

characters.name: Hotep-Ra
characters.description: A mummy-like ghost who's the spirit of the minion of King Duulaman, an Ancient Egyptian pharaoh who looked exactly like Tucker. He is awoken when Tucker looks into the mirror on his sarcophagus, and immediately declares himself as Tucker's loyal servant. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He presents himself as a loyal and selfless servant to Tucker, when in actuality, he's manipulating him for his own end. British Teeth: His teeth are white, but are notably crooked and misaligned. Death-Based Ghost Powers: He is the soul/spirit of the minion of an ancient Egyptian pharaoh and appears as askeletalMummycovered in bandages. Power-wise, he hasMummy WrapandSand Blasterabilities. Dem Bones: Hotep-Ra is just a skeleton beneath his mummy bandages.

characters.name: Nocturn
characters.description: The ghost of sleep, Nocturn has the power to put people to sleep and harvests the dreams of humans. Celestial Body: With the exception of his head, Nocturn's body looks like a shapeless mass in a vaguely humanoid form cut out from a starry night. Deadpan Snarker:Nocturn:I believe this is when I say "Dream on!" Dream Stealer:Downplayed. Nocturn feeds off the dreams to grow stronger, but he doesn't remove them. Dream Weaver: It's uncertain whether or not this is Nocturn's own power, or if his headgear does it, but it puts people in their fantasies too much to be a coincidence either way.

characters.name: Prince Aragon
characters.description: Prince Aragon is the ruthless and cruel older brother of Princess Dorathea (AKA The Dragon Ghost), both of whom appeared to have lived in the Middle Ages (the 4th to the 16th centuries). 0% Approval Rating: He's despised by everyone in the area of ghost zone ruled by him. Aloof Older Brother: And abusive. Poor Dorathea. And Now You Must Marry Me: Tried to force Sam into being his bride. Bad Boss: He's verbally abusive towards his sister, even though she initially assists him with his plans. It's suggested that he's a tyrant towards his entire kingdom as well.

characters.name: The Archer Ghost and the Executioner Ghost
characters.description: Prince Aragon's silent minions. The Executioner Ghost uses an axe to attack his foes, while the Archer Ghost uses a bow and arrow. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear if they follow Prince Aragon out of loyalty, or out of fear like Dorathea and the rest of his subjects. Co-Dragons: Both share the role of being Prince Aragon's minions. The Executioner: Given his name, the Executioner Ghost probably functions as an executioner in Prince Aragon's kingdom. In the Hood: The Archer Ghost's head is constantly hidden in a hood, leaving only his green eyes visible.

characters.name: Undergrowth
characters.description: A plant ghost who wants to destroy civilization due to the harm they brought to his "children". Advertised Extra: Undergrowth was advertised a lot as a major villain to the show when the episode was being promoted (especially when it came to the video game adapation of the episode), but he only had one major episode that was only a half hour long. Contrast to Dark Danny where he was the main villian for a hour long special). The Bad Guy Wins: The Nick.com gameUrban Jungle Rumbleends with Undergrowth winning should you beat the game while playing as him or Vegetized Sam.The same ending happens should you lose as Danny or Frostbite. Botanical Abomination: He seems to be the spectral embodiment ofGaia's Vengeanceand the Plant Kingdom, his body a monstrous plant creature in a vaguely humanoid form and command over plant-life. Brainwashed and Crazy: Inflicts this onSam, making her his "daughter".

characters.name: Vortex
characters.description: A powerful spirit that can control the weather. Delusions of Eloquence: As shown by hisLarge Hamquote below, he sees himself as aMad Artisttype, comparing his weather disasters to the Mona Lisa, yet as Vlad points out, he got the wrong artist.Vlad:That wasDa Vinci, you dolt.Vortex:Whatever. Ghostly Wail: Vortex can let loose a ghostly sonic shriek, a sub-power of the above-mentioned Ghostly Wail but Vortex is only extremely less powerful. Large Ham: "'Stop the rain'?! The weather is my art! I will not just 'stop it'! Did anyone askPicassoto stop painting the Mona Lisa!?" Pride: His fatal flaw. He is manipulated into returning to Amity Park, where Danny can defeat him, after Sam and Tucker tell him that there's one spot on earth where even he can't alter the weather and he decides to prove them wrong.

characters.name: Jack Fenton
characters.description: Danny's bumbling father, Jack Fenton has a massive hatred of ghosts and is an obsessive inventor of ghost weaponry and gadgets, designed to rip them apartmolecule by moleculewithout trial. Naturally, this usually results in a panicky Danny Phantom whom Jack considers as one of his enemies, despite having saved the world countless times. Tends to be clueless, but can briefly turn into aBadass Normalif his loved ones are threatened. Achievements in Ignorance: Not only did he manage to build technology that can harm ghosts despite not having seen one until the last few minutes of "Mystery Meat", he also unintentionally developed the means for two normal humans to be infused with ecto-energy and gain superpowers (something he and his wife dismissed as impossible). Acrofatic: Surprisingly athletic for a man of his girth. Action Dad: Always eager to hunt ghosts, regardless of whether or not he's capable of it. Always Someone Better: After experiencing the “Maddie Masters” timeline, Danny gained a newfound respect for his father not just for being a better man than Vlad, but a better husband too.

characters.name: Maddie Fenton
characters.description: Equally obsessed with ghost hunting and research as her husband Jack, Maddie nevertheless remains far more logical, competent, and calmer then her husband. She is the main romantic target for Vlad. The Ace: Maddie is shown to be a very skilled ghost hunter, she even manages to fight off a whole pack of ghost animals, single handily while protecting Danny. In "Public Enemies", Danny even acknowledges that his mom is alegitimatethreat towards ghosts, compared to his bumbling father. Action Mom: Maddie is aninth degree martial artist! Amazingly Embarrassing Parent: Her and Jack's ghost-hunting craze causes Danny and Jazz a lot of embarrassment. It's also implied to be partly why Danny is looked down on and considered an outcast by his peers. Arbitrary Skepticism: It's revealed in "The Fright Before Christmas" she's gotten into annual fights with Jack to disprove the existence of Santa, despite that she spends her time building weapons to fightghosts.

characters.name: Dani Fenton/Dani Phantom
characters.description: Danny's clone, created by Vlad as a stepping stone to the perfect Danny Fenton/Phantom clone to call as his own son. Unlike the various other Danny clones, Danielle has a mind of her own, possessing a naive behavior with much of Danny's traits and character. She is often childish and spunky, but well-meaning. An imperfect clone, she is constantly dissolving and has to keep her powers in check. She and Danny grow close, with Dannystanding up for her without hesitation. Aborted Arc: According toWord of God, had the series continued afterPhantom Planet, Jack and Maddiewould've adopted Dani as their daughter, making her Jazz and Danny's younger sister. Affectionate Nickname: Insists on being called Dani, with an I. Annoying Younger Sibling: Danny seemed to treat Danielle as one at first, albeit more from not trusting her than anything else. He gets over this when he learns what she actually is. Artificial Family Member: She was created in a botched attempt to clone Danny, but he accepts her as family. Although he calls her his cousin, it'd be more accurate to call her a genetic twin sister.

characters.name: Alicia
characters.description: Maddie's sister, Danny and Jazz's aunt, and Jack's sister-in-law. She is divorced and lives in a cabin in Spittoon, Arkansas. Big Sister Instinct: While it's not certain if she's Maddie's big sister or not, she does love Maddie and only wants what is best for her, despite her bitterness and temper, and she is understandably upset when Jack procrastinates in apologizing to her. Does Not Like Men: Somewhat, she is divorced and claims that the divorce was the best decision of her life. She even celebrates the anniversary of her divorce. Given that the rest of her community joins in the festivities, she likely has her reasons. Jerkass Has a Point: Gruff as she is, she isn’t wrong that Jack’s ghost obsession makes him neglect Maddie (including forgetting their anniversary for the 18th time) and he’s very foolish. She’s also understandably peeved at Jack for wasting his time apologizing. Obnoxious In-Laws: She does not like Jack and the feeling is mutual.

characters.name: Jeremy and Pamela Manson
characters.description: Sam's rich, stuck-up, controlling parents. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: In their mind, they mean well. However, it's clear Sam genuinely wishes her parents weren't so obsessed with what she did and let her have some independence. Dramatically Missing the Point: They see Danny (and possibly Tucker in some extent) as a bad influence and the source of Sam's obsession with all things Goth. While Danny's parents have given them some trouble that would cause the couple to be wary of him, they don't see the obvious reasons why Dannywouldn’tbe the cause of Sam being a Goth, like how he doesn't dress in Goth clothes. They can't see Sam is acting out because ofhow controlling they are. Hollywood Genetics: If it weren't for a photo of her grandmother Ida having black hair, one would assume Sam was adopted by Jeremy and Pamela. Her black hair could, in theory, be hair-dye, though neither her parents nor her grandmother have purple eyes. Idle Rich: Sam's comment in "Control Freaks" implies that neither of her parents work in real jobs and instead "work" as super-optimistic socialites.

characters.name: Ida Manson
characters.description: Sam's paternal grandmother and Jeremy's mother. Cool Old Lady: Unlike Jeremy and Pamela, she's more understanding of Sam and accepts her for who she is, having been a non-conformist herself in her youth. She even allows Sam to sneak out of their house to go save Danny anddisguises herself as Samto ward off suspicion. It's no surprise that Sam gets along with her better than her parents. Early-Bird Cameo: She was first mentioned by Sam in "Parental Bonding" and made two cameo appearances before she's confirmed to be Sam's grandmother in "Control Freak". Good Grandparents: She's very understanding towards her granddaughter, and accepts her wholeheartedly due to being much like her when Ida was in her youth. I Was Quite a Looker: As seen in an old picture of her, she used to be a very pretty young woman.

characters.name: Maurice and Angela Foley
characters.description: All There in the Script: Although Maurice's name was revealed in "Forever Phantom", Angela is never mentioned by name, yet is confirmed to be "Angela" in the end credits. Failed a Spot Check: In "Life Lessons", Angela baked cookies for a bake sale. She failed to make note that the flour she used were for a school project that her son was looking after, namely the diapers and smiley faces that most flour sacks don't have. Flat Characters: There's no episode that solely focuses on Tucker and his parents, much like how "Control Freaks" delved deep into Sam's relationship with her own parents. Good Parents: Unlike Sam and her more controlling parents, Tucker appears to have a good relationship with his folks. Although Tucker's mom is pretty stern with her son's technology obsession (as shown briefly in "Flirting with Disaster" when she asks him if he's online again), she doesn't appear to be overly controlling about it and is implied to be accepting of him. Strong Family Resemblance: Maurice looks like an almost exact copy of his son outside of hair and a mustache, with nothing from Angela present in Tucker's appearance.

characters.name: Damon Gray
characters.description: Valerie's father and head of R&D at Axion Labs, but was temporarily demoted to a security guard following the Ghost Dog incident. Fantastic Racism: Seems to have shades of this towards ghosts as shown in "Flirting with Disaster". He open fires at Danny Phantom anddoesn't believe him when he warns the Grays about Technus. Locked Out of the Loop: He's unaware that Valerie got her ghost equipment from Vlad. Papa Wolf: Is quite protective of Valerie, and even more so when he learns she's become a ghost hunter. Parental Obliviousness: Was kept in the dark about his daughter's new ghost-hunting lifestyle, at least untilReign Stormwhen Danny pulls off aDramatic Unmaskand reveals Valerie's identity to Damon. After which, he tries to forbid his daughter from hunting ghosts by locking her gear away for her safety and becomes annoyed whenever she uses them.

characters.name: Valerie Gray
characters.description: Valerie started off as theRich Bitchbefore a ghost dog (with Danny in tow) cost her father his job, forcing her to lead a poor, unpopular existence. She was given advanced ghost weapons fromVlad Mastersby mail and used them to exact her revenge. She eventuallymakes it a full time jobwith Danny Phantom as her primary target. She grows to see the world beyond her once shallow view and eventually develops aromantic interestwith Danny Fenton, unaware of his alter ego. Aborted Arc: It's obvious they meant to wrap up her storyline with Vlad more neatly, but thanks to the sudden cancellation, not so much. She just gets a brief mention and a non-speaking cameo in "Phantom Planet",where she and her dad are part of the Arctic Team dealing with the Disasteroid and learn Danny Phantom'sSecret Identity. Action Girl: Valerie makes it her life's work to take out any ghost she comes across, especially the Ghost Boy. Alpha Bitch: Used to be this while she was rich and popular,notably sending Kwan after Danny after he accidentally caused Paulina to spill her coffee on Valerie's new shirt. Even while she's slowly but surely growing out of this, Sam is quick to remind Valerie just how rotten she's acted towards her and her friends back then.Valerie herself seems to realize this. Anti-Hero: She begins her ghost career specifically to get revenge on the ghosts she held responsible for her ruined life. Her actions start to become more noble in time, but many of her deep-seated prejudices remain.

characters.name: Dash Baxter
characters.description: Standard issue bullying jock who on the outside is the typical menacing antagonist in Danny's school while deep inside, he portrays a far more sensitive soul, used mostly for laughs. Abhorrent Admirer: The opening of "Attack of the Killer Garage Sale" has him fawning over Jazz and later inviting her to his party. Not only is she annoyed by him since he didn't listen to her tutoring him, she evidently didn't take kindly to him being mean to Danny. She only agreed to go if Danny was invited, but revealed to Danny she had no intention of going at all. In "Frightmare", she had a nightmare of being married to Dash. He also hits on Paulina and Ember, who are likewise irritated by his affection. Advertised Extra: He appears in the theme song, locking Danny in his locker before Danny uses his powers to turn the tables on him. Dash himself isn't a relevant character to the show outside of small bits, and is only important in at least two episodes. He's also been absent in far more episodes than the ones where he has any importance to the plot. Alpha Bastard: Although a quintessentialJerk Jock, he also has a lot ofAlpha Bitch-like qualities to him. He's the leader of both the A-Listers and his owngang of fellow jocks, is implied to be well-off, throws exclusive parties, and along with physically bullying Danny, he also verbally bullies him (and occasionally also Tucker and Sam) by insulting him at nearly every chance he gets. In addition, his ostracization of anyone below a certain level of wealth or popularity, his ditching of Valerie as a friend for not meeting these standards, hisBitch in Sheep's Clothingbehavior towards the adults, and his efforts to humiliate Danny in certain episodes (like "Fright Night" for example) definitely give him the same energy as a petty and spiteful mean girl. The Bad Guy Wins: There are a few episodes where he ends up getting the last laugh over Danny, notably in "Fright Night" and "Reign Storm".

characters.name: Kwan
characters.description: Dash's best friend and fellow jock who, while having jerk jock tendencies himself, is a lot nicer than Dash and the other popular kids. Asian Airhead: He's of Asian descent and is aDumb Jocklike Dash (though he becomesAsian and Nerdyin theBad Futureshown inThe Ultimate Enemy). Best Friend: He’s best friends with Dash. Beta Couple: Implied to be one with Star. Dirty Coward: Just like Dash, he’ll pick on kids who are a lot smaller than him, but he’ll flee in terror if he sees a ghost.

characters.name: Paulina Sanchez
characters.description: A girl Danny held a crush on before he wised up and moved on. She's the standard issueAlpha Bitchand like all stereotypes like her, tends to victimize the less popular girls and focus primary on shallow mannerisms. She harbors a crush on Danny Phantom, but won't give Danny Fenton the time of day. Accidental Misnaming: To Danny’s annoyance, she used to call Danny’s superhero alter-ego "Inviso-Bill" (the stupid nickname the cops came up with for him) since everyone in Amity Park thought that was his name. She stops after "Reign Storm", since Danny told everyone his hero name is Danny Phantom. Alpha Bitch: The most popular girl in school and loves to rub it in people's faces. In her debut episode, she wanted to get back at Sam for calling her shallow, so she agreed to go on a date with Danny solely because she believed she was stealing him from Sam. After Sam tells her she doesn’t want to date Danny, Paulina decides she’s going to dump Danny in front of the school and humiliate him. Bait the Dog:Played Within the episode "Memory Blank". Paulina invites Danny, Sam, and Tucker to her 15th birthday party solely because she always sees the ghost boy around them. She's upfront about the fact that she's only inviting Danny and his friends because she wants Danny Phantom to be there, and she still sees the trio as losers, which she doesn't even bother to try and hide from them. While her motives are selfish, she says it in a way that is at least honest and doesn't seem like she'd mind their presence. Danny seems more than happy to attend her party and fulfill her request. Later on, however, when Danny Phantom saves Paulina from one of the ghosts that are after her, she tries to use this chance to invite him to her party and specifically states that this means she can also un-invite human Danny and his friends (much to Danny's shock). While not outright stated, it's implied that this is the point where Danny starts to lose interest in Paulina because of that and for acting so

characters.name: Star
characters.description: Paulina's best friend and"satellite". Art Evolution: By the later portion of Season 2, her design is given minor changes. Her eyelashes aren't visible, her nose isn't as round and the "9" on her shirt disappears. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: In a few episodes, she is seen wearing an orange dress that shows off her midriff. Beauty Is Bad: She's pretty like Paulina, but is a jerk to the unpopular students. Beta Bitch: She mostly hangs around with Paulina to maintain some popularity. In "Lucky in Love", Sam and Tucker outright refer to her as a "satellite", being "the marginally attractive girl who always orbits around the popular girl".

characters.name: Elliot
characters.description: A foreign exchange student from Hungary visiting Amity Park under the name "Gregor" and Sam's second love interest. He's later revealed to be an American boy from Michigan. Derailing Love Interest: Gregor exists purely to throw an obstacle between the hero and his official love interest in one episode. Fauxreigner: Hungarian "Gregor" is actually just a kid from Michigan named Elliot who made up the name, accent, and background just to impress Sam. Naturally, Sam dumps him for it. I'm a Man; I Can't Help It: When Sam calls Elliot out for lying to her and her friends the whole time, he claims this is the reason why he's done it, prompting Sam to dump him on the spot.Sam: Wait a minute... you werefakingit?! The accent, and liking Tucker, just to get on my good side?Elliot: Agh, I'm aguy!Hello! I mean, I really like you, but come on![gestures to Tucker, who frowns at Sam as if saying, "You're seriously gonna keep hanging out with this jerk?"][Cue to Sam giving Elliot an unamusedDeath Glare]Elliot: ...We're through, aren't we?Sam: Oh,beyond.Elliot: Oh well. Innocently Insensitive: He seems aware that Danny likes Sam as more than a friend, hence his jealousy towards them hanging out. Gregor straight up tells Danny to his face that he's going to ask Sam to go steady with him (to Danny's horror).

characters.name: Mikey
characters.description: A geeky kid who's constantly picked on by the jocks at Casper High. Bookworm: He’s usually seen carrying books and is smart enough to do all the A-Listers' homework for them. Butt-Monkey: Can't catch a break with the school bullies, and once got glued to a wall and gagged by Skulker after asking nicely if he could use the computer the ghost was studying. The Dog Bites Back: In "Memory Blank", Mikey wishes he could show Dash and Kwan what being stuffed into a locker feels like. Desiree grants his wish, turning him into a monster, and he stuffs the bullies into the locker before turning back into a human and quickly closing the locker.Mikey: I rock! Even Nerds Have Standards: Despite being very nerdy himself, he thinks Tucker isn’t cool enough to talk to him.

characters.name: Mr. Lancer
characters.description: The primary teacher (and vice-principal) of Casper High who tends to favor the popular kids, especially Dash. Often strict with an inability to connect with his students, Mr. Lancer may seem like a bullying mentor to Danny, but deep down, he wants all his students to succeed, so that he can satisfy his own ego. Adults Are Useless:Deliberately and unfairly turns a blind eye to Dash Baxter’s bullying solely because he’s a football star and is therefore "exempt from scorn".Though he seemed of have grown out of it somewhat in the Halloween episode, he's still pretty unfair. When Dash is about to hit Danny, he initially intended to punish BOTH for "having a fight" (even though Dash was clearly the one intending to hit Danny). Then, he has them compete to make the best haunted house to determine who doesn't get punished and laterspitefullymakes Dash the winner (when he initially declared it a tie) after Jack and Maddieaccidentally embarrass him.There's also the fact that inThe Ultimate Enemy, consideringLancer's methods, he uses scare tactics likeService Sector Stereotypeson his students that they’ll be sent to work at the Nasty Burger if they fail on the C.A.T., rather than actually encouraging them to try their best. Deliberately and unfairly turns a blind eye to Dash Baxter’s bullying solely because he’s a football star and is therefore "exempt from scorn". Though he seemed of have grown out of it somewhat in the Halloween episode, he's still pretty unfair. When Dash is about to hit Danny, he initially intended to punish BOTH for "having a fight" (even though Dash was clearly the one intending to hit Danny). Then, he has them compete to make the best haunted house to determine who doesn't get punished and laterspitefullymakes Dash the winner (when he initially declared it a tie) after Jack and Maddieaccidentally embarrass him. There's also the fact that inThe Ultimate Enemy, consideringLancer's methods, he uses scare tactics likeService Sector Stereotypeson his student

characters.name: Ms. Tetslaff
characters.description: The gym teacher at Casper High. Brawn Hilda: She's a huge, muscular, mannish woman with a deep voice. Gym Class Hell: Her class seems to be terrible for the students, at least judging by what little we see of it. Hypocritical Humor: In "Micromanagement", she preaches to the students about being fit while alsochowing down on a foot-long sub, something Tucker lampshades.Tucker: Apparently, somebody doesn't own a mirror.[Gets knocked down by a weight ball thrown by Tetslaff]Danny: And apparently somebody doesn't have a sense of humor. Sadist Teacher: She delights in tormenting the students, such as when she berates Danny and Tucker over their inability to pass the Presidential Fitness Exam and then assigns them tutors to force them through rigorous workouts in order to improve.

characters.name: Principal Ishiyama
characters.description: The principal of Casper High. Apathetic Teacher: While she at least doesn't go out of her way to torment her students likeMr. Lancer, it's clear she's not a good principal in the slightest, not so much from what we see of her appearances given that it's few and far between, but moreso from what isimplied. She does nothing to curb the bullying at Casper High or discipline the football team for their bullying. Despite being Mr. Lancer's boss, she also does nothing about his blatant favoritism towards the popular students and allows both Mr. Lancer and Coach Teslaff to get away with beingSadist Teacherstowards their students. Also, given her very little appearances as well as the fact that Mr. Lancer does most of the work in bossing around the students, she's seemingly not involved in her job as a principal that much."Public Enemies" does show that sheiswilling to take measures to protect students from ghost attacks. Granted, said "measures" are through strict rules that limit the students' freedom. "Public Enemies" does show that sheiswilling to take measures to protect students from ghost attacks. Granted, said "measures" are through strict rules that limit the students' freedom. Flat Character: Because she lacks appearances in the series, her personality isn't fleshed out that much. Put on a Bus: Is never seen nor mentioned in season 2 and 3, despite being the principal of Casper High.

characters.name: Mr. Falluca
characters.description: A teacher of an unknown subject at Casper High. Admiring the Abomination: "Doctor's Disorders" starts with him staring at Spectra’s huge ghost mosquito and remarking "Fascinating. Possibly some of the most interesting mandibular formations I’ve ever seen." However, his fascination turns to fear when the ghost mosquito starts growling at him. Flat Character: Doesn't have any significant role in the series and only makes a few appearances such as "Doctor's Disorders" and "Flirting with Disaster".

characters.name: Masters' Blasters
characters.description: In the series finale, Vlad finances a group of three teenagers to hunt ghosts as revenge for Danny constantly humiliating him. Action Girl: Vid is just as capable as Thrash and takes to the field. Everyone Has Standards:Once the Masters' Blasters find out Vlad is a half-ghost supervillain, they look horrified andimmediatelyturn on their boss,but are easily defeated by him. Greed: They aren't villains, but they're definitely less heroic than Danny is, given they insist on getting paid as soon as they save someone. Kid Heroes: Teen variants. Par the course for the show, and invoked by Vlad to compare them to Danny Phantom.

characters.name: Lance Thunder
characters.description: Amity's local weather man, who often finds himself in ghost-related dangerous circumstances. '80s Hair: A huge blonde coif. Deadpan Snarker: "Wishing he'd taken that job in Chicago, this is Lance Thunder, Action News!" Mad Libs Catchphrase: "Not the (insert body part)!" Meaningful Name: He's a weatherman called LanceThunder. He shares this trait with his co-worker Tiffany Snow.

characters.name: Ernesto Montez
characters.description: Former mayor of Amity Park until season 3 when Vlad Masters takes his place. Attention Whore: He only attends a meeting in Casper High for the photo opportunity and to get more votes. Fantastic Racism: Although it's implied that Walker influenced the mayor's hatred for ghosts while overshadowing him, he still declares Danny Phantom 'Public Ghost Enemy #1' after the events of "Public Enemies", even after being freed from Walker's control, and has it in forallghosts.His racism towards ghosts becomes more evident at the end ofA Glitch In Time, at least in the timeline where his knowledge of Danny's identity is erased. Montez declares Amity Park an "anti-ghost" city, allows mandatory ghost-hunting classes in schools, creates an official branch for ghost hunters in politics and such, and once again decrees Danny Phantom and all ghosts menaces to humanity. His racism towards ghosts becomes more evident at the end ofA Glitch In Time, at least in the timeline where his knowledge of Danny's identity is erased. Montez declares Amity Park an "anti-ghost" city, allows mandatory ghost-hunting classes in schools, creates an official branch for ghost hunters in politics and such, and once again decrees Danny Phantom and all ghosts menaces to humanity. Put on a Bus: Is never seen on-screen again after his debut in "Public Enemies". While he's pictured in "Eye for an Eye", he's never seen giving his own speech during Amity Park's election day, and is eventually outvoted by Vlad as mayor.Montez makes his full re-appearanceinA Glitch in Time, where he's mayor again after Vlad's banishment.

characters.name: Mr. Sanchez
characters.description: Boyfriend-Blocking Dad: While hedoesallow Danny to date Paulina, he doesn’t seem happy about it. Dude in Distress: Becomes one of the many adults kidnapped by Youngblood in "Pirate Radio". Hair-Trigger Temper: He is provoked by the mere presence of Danny without him really doing anything other than dating his daughter. Irony: He is concerned about his daughter being hurt by Danny, when ironically Paulina herself would be the one to break Danny’s heart at the end of his debut episode. Mugging the Monster: Terrorizes Danny during their brief interaction while unaware of the fact that Danny has superpowers, who at that point was already proven to be competent enough to defeat ghosts including the fairly powerful Lunch Lady.Played With, since even with his ghost powers, Danny is still very much intimidated by him due to the man being a much larger adult.

characters.name: Clockwork
characters.description: The ghost of time, Clockwork keeps the flow of time and interferes when he feels something is disturbing said flow. He is mysterious and powerful, knowing every aspect of time: past, present, and future. He remains a neutral influence in Danny's life, playing only by his rules. He doesn't perceive time as a linear sequence of events; this is reflected in his appearance, which constantly fluctuates in age. All-Powerful Bystander: Clockwork is the master of all time and has the ability to do pretty much whatever he wants with it. He also knows everything. Despite this, he rarely intervenes and is a fairly neutral character, though he's willing to intervene if the situation is dire enough. Batman Gambit: Clockwork pulled one off so perfectly in "The Ultimate Enemy", no one was aware he was a good guy until the end. Big Damn Heroes: During the climax ofThe Ultimate Enemyhe rescues Sam, Tucker, Jazz, Maddie, Jack and Lancer from the explosion of the Nasty Burger, as a reward forDanny's determination to not become the evil he was originally supposed to become. Big Good: Even taking his neutrality in consideration, he’s as close to one for Team Phantom, acting as the one who oversees the flow of time and only directly intervene if something is a huge enough threat, such asDark Danny.

characters.name: Frostbite
characters.description: A giant Yeti-like ghost, leader of the Far Frozen realm, and an all-around(n)ice guy. He eventually becomes Danny's mentor after the latter manifests ice powers. Ancient Keeper: Frostbite is the protecter of the Infi-Map, an ancient map of the Ghost Zone that can lead to any entrance and through time itself. An Arm and a Leg: One of his arms is skeletal and covered in ice as a sort of prosthetic. No other member of the Far Frozen has these. Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and Yeti: He and his race appear to be some form of yeti. Blue Means Cold: His ice beams are colored blue.

characters.name: Dairy King
characters.description: The former owner of Vlad's mansion, the Dairy King was once a successful bussinessman in the dairy industry. After his death, his ghost now haunts his former home. The Dairy King is one of the first friendly ghosts Danny encounters. Always Chaotic Evil: Subverted. He is the first ghost Danny encounters who isn't hostile. Ambiguously Related: In the alternate timeline, Vlad is still living in the same castle because he's the successor to the Dairy King. The Dairy King might in fact be a relative of his, though this is never brought up. Big Damn Heroes: Danny is trapped inside Skulker's contraption and has no way in stopping Vlad from humiliating his father. Then, the Dairy King arrives and let him out. Big Fun: He is a rather obese man who speaks in a jolly and pleasant way.

characters.name: Cujo
characters.description: The puppy ghost of one of Axion Labs' guard dogs who takes a liking to Danny. When enraged, he becomes larger and much more monstrous. Canine Companion: Was the closest thing Danny had to a pet in "Shades of Gray". Face–Monster Turn: While he doesn't usually mean any harm, his feral and aggressive personality often causes Danny problems in his large dog form, even to the point of occasionally attacking him or his friends. Even when he's more benevolent he can be difficult for Danny to keep under control. Hulking Out: Becomes a much larger and frightening dog when angered, though his fondness for Danny remains (usually). In-Series Nickname: "Cujo" isn't actually his name, just something Danny once called him. Fandom has stuck with it.

characters.name: Princess Dorathea
characters.description: A ghostly princess who can transform into a dragon at will. She lives in a section of the Ghost Zone ruled by her evil brother Prince Aragon. In her first appearances, she's furious and upset because apparently her mother doesn't allow her to go to a costume ball. In her second main appearance, she's an unwilling pawn to her brother, to whom she's been submissive all her life, but she learns to overcome her fear of him. Abhorrent Admirer: At the end of her debut episode, she seems to develop a crush on Tucker, who is uncomfortable with her advances. This isn't brought up in her later appearances, and she outright calls him annoying in "Beauty Marked". Ambiguously Human: We see a painting of her as a human, implying she used to be one, but it's later shown that she can disguise herself as human, meaning it could have been painted while she was incognito. On the other hand, it's apaintingand not a photo, so it could be inaccurate. Anti-Villain: In her first main appearance, she causes trouble for Danny and his friends, but she's not actually evil. In her second, she's initially presented as a serious antagonist, but it's eventually revealed she's only doing her brother's bidding because she's forced to. Cain and Abel: She's a good ghost who falls victim to her evil brother Aragon, who abuses her and forces her to do whatever he wants.

characters.name: Pandora
characters.description: The guardian of Pandora's Box. Action Girl: A female ghost with some powerful abilities and great fighting skills. Adaptational Badass: The Pandora of myth was a mere mortal who opened the box after being given it by the gods. In this show, she has godlike power herself and created the box in the first place to imprison all the evil it ended up containing. The Dreaded: She's pretty well-known in the Ghost Zone, and even Skulker seems to fear her. Multi-Armed and Dangerous: She possesses two pairs of arms.

characters.name: Wulf
characters.description: An Esperanto-speaking werewolf ghost who was one of Walker's prisoners. Promised freedom if he helps capture Danny Phantom, he instead becomes friends with the Ghost Boy. Absurdly Sharp Claws: His claws are so sharp, he can even cut through Ghost Shields. Because You Were Nice to Me: Befriends Team Phantom because they freed him from Walker. The Big Guy: Is a large werewolf-ghost, and between that and hisDimensional Cutterclaws is easily among Danny's more powerful allies. Boxed Crook: What he debuts as. What he did to get himself sentenced isn't known, but knowingWalker, it might've just been for looking funny.

characters.name: Behemoth
characters.description: A giant monster ghost who guards the Skeleton Key. Breath Weapon: He is able to breathe a large stream of purple fire as a long range attack. In-Series Nickname: Vlad refers to it as "Behemoth", but it's unclear if that's the ghost's official name or if Vlad just called it that based on its appearance. Killer Gorilla: It is a poweful ghost with ape-like features. MacGuffin Guardian: It guards the Skeleton Key.

characters.name: Klemper
characters.description: A big, annoying ghost who continually whines that he wants friends. Beware the Silly Ones: It's easy to mistake him for a harmless oaf, but he's not to be underestimated. He manages to hold his own in fights with Danny, and he defeats a large number of Pariah Dark's soldiers single-handedly inReign Storm. Butt-Monkey: Everyone who meets Klemper can’t stand him and refuses to be his friend. Desperately Craves Affection: This is his entire personality. Dumb Muscle: His ice powers and great strength are a menace, but he's stupid and oafish.

characters.name: Maddie the Cat
characters.description: Vlad's pet cat, which he insists is his sister's. Amplified Animal Aptitude: In her first appearance, Maddie acts like a real cat, Vlad only projecting what he wants to hear. In her later appearances, she seems smart enough to make suggestions to Vlad or express dislike of something. Brick Joke: Back in "Maternal Instincts", Vlad insists he will not get a cat like Danny mockingly suggested. Cats Are Mean: In her first appearance, she was more innocent and averted this. Later, she plays this straight. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In her first appearance, she was a short-haired domestic kitten, but later she's an adult Persian.

characters.name: Delilah
characters.description: An endangered purple-back gorilla Danny once studied for an extra credit biology assignment in "One of a Kind". Was formerly known as Sampson while mistaken as a male. Gentle Gorilla: Initially. Whenever feeling threatened by something like Skulker, she goes full-onKiller Gorillamode and gives Skulker aNo-Holds-Barred Beatdowntwicein their encounters. However, she's gentle and peaceful around Danny when he's in ghost mode, even trying to flee when he flies after her to put her back. Intelligent Primate: Was able to tell that Skulker is bad news and saw Danny and his friends as no threats as she always acts peaceful around them. Meaningful Name: Her original name, Sampson, refers to theBiblicalfigure Samson who was known for his immense strength, which is fitting for a strong animal like a gorilla. However, after Danny discovers that she's actually female, her name is changed to Delilah, who was Samson's lover. Samus Is a Girl: It turns out that "Sampson" is actually a female gorilla now renamed "Delilah" and with that knowledge, she can continue the species with the other male gorilla. Mr. Lancer is surprised why nobody ever considered checking the gorilla more closely beforehand.Mr. Lancer:Nobody at that zoo ever bothered to see if it was a boy or a girl?Danny:It's weird, huh? Well, maybe they were respecting her privacy.
